title: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean?
rawText:
OpenAI released solutions to three blockbuster math problems that have long vexed researchers yesterday. One was a surprise rejection of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), a durable assumption in computer science that plays a large role in how we understand what is difficult to compute.
As with previous proof-drops from the frontier lab, scientific communities responded with a mixture of thrill and dismay. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge suggested that OpenAI was basing its solutions from pre-existing work, and hours later, Anthropic subsequently released its own refutation of ETH.
However, OpenAI’s process is evolving. This time, the lab structured its releases differently for each of the three disciplines involved: Mathematicians got the work dropped on GitHub; the computer scientists formed a working group, asked for the proofs to be shared publicly and OpenAI to fund a conference to discuss them; the physicists formed a working group that will determine how their result will be released.
MIT Professor Ryan Williams is the computer scientist who is organizing his field’s response to the new finding. Williams, whose work focuses on these questions of computational complexity, has criticized OpenAI’s approach in the past, calling its proof dump earlier this October a “DDOS attack on mathematicians.”
However, he agreed to collaborate with the frontier labs in order to help shepherd ideas that are vital to the field, he told TechCrunch. The lab asked him to help interpret the solution, along with UC San Diego computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who first published the ETH in 1999.
Their first step was to release an open letter calling for feedback from scientists interested in these problems and a discussion of the norms around AI contributions to their work.
“Some parts [of OpenAI’s proof] are, maybe you could say routine, but then yes, there are two or three alien-looking parts, and it’s exactly these parts that that I saw that made me think, wow, this is something that the whole community needs to work on together,” Williams told TechCrunch.
Are you down with P vs NP?
The ETH is part of a broader class of problems known as P vs NP, which has animated computer science and many other fields for decades. Reductively, researchers are trying to understand if any problem whose solution can be easily verified (NP) can also be easily solved (P).
A simple example is the game Sodoku: Once a solution to a puzzle is in place, it can be quickly verified, but finding the solution is time-consuming. That dynamic is true across a range of important problems, and the insight underpins cryptographic systems: When you have the key to an encoded message, you can reveal it, but actually cracking an effective code takes too long to be useful.
However, scientists have yet to prove whether that is always true. “P = NP is saying that, not only can you verify Sudoku solutions when they exist, you can just generate them,” Williams said. “P = NP is asserting that this is true for every single problem you can verify quickly — if you can verify it quickly, you can solve it quickly. So this just seems too good to be true.”
That’s why most scientists assume that P ≠ NP. ETH provided evidence for that. It basically says that even the fastest computer algorithm needs exponentially more time to find a solution as the number of variables grow in a specific class of tricky logic puzzle.
The claims from OpenAI and Anthropic is that their models have come up with algorithms that solve those puzzles in “sub-exponential” time, meaning faster than the speeds previously thought possible. If true, they may have proven the EFT to be false — refuted it, in scientific terms — and maybe opened up a path for algorithms that generally perform P = NP.
“Every computer scientist should probably put a little more weight on the plausibility of P = NP, but one’s weight may vary,” Williams said. “I do think that it kind of calls into question a lot of the intuitions that we thought we had about … how tractable [hard NP problems] are. I also think that this is probably not the final answer either. I don’t think that OpenAI’s algorithm could possibly be the best algorithm you can get.”
The work ahead for computer scientists
The durability of ETH has lead to it being included in many scientific papers over the past decade that will need to be revisited if the AI labs claims that they’ve proven it wrong holds up, Williams said.
“This is partly why I was asking or pushing OpenAI to support a conference on this — it’s going to affect many researchers’ works, and we need to figure out, okay, what happens next besides understanding the algorithms. We need to understand, how should the foundations change compared to what we had before?” he said.
Before scientific concerns, there are cybersecurity questions. Williams said that an improved algorithm could imply that cryptographic systems relying on certain key sizes could be considered broken. So one of the first questions he asked OpenAI science lead Dan Roberts “was if they had checked that this affects any crypto systems … is anything insecure now? And apparently, they checked, and they were reasonably confident that this didn’t … imply any breaks.”
This new AI paradigm of scientific discovery is still a work in progress, but Williams says he is optimistic despite real concerns, particularly about training the next generation of scientists. Being a computer scientist who does high level math has perhaps made the adjustment easier for him than for pure mathematicians.
Still, he says AI is “forcing people to be a little more ambitious about the kind of work that they do, and to think more deeply about, okay, if all the things I used to work on are now low hanging fruit for AI, how can I raise the bar for the kind of scientific questions I want to ask?”

title: Google’s Genie 4 world model adds audio, more realistic worlds, and real-time steering
rawText:
Google DeepMind released its newest world model, Genie 4, in research preview on Tuesday. The latest model generates the most photorealistic and interactive worlds yet, allowing users to type prompts mid-simulation to change the scene. The model also generates real-time audio that matches the simulated world, including music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue.
The release of Genie 4 comes a couple of months after AI video startup Runway released its second world model, GWM Worlds 2, a playable model that responds dynamically to user inputs and includes audio generation. At the same time, the world model industry is beginning to consolidate. Fei-Fei Li’s World Labs is being acquired by AMD, Amazon is in talks to buy Decart, and Rivian just acquired Third Dimension to bring simulation capabilities in-house for self-driving testing.
Genie 4 is Google’s latest move to stay ahead in the crowded field.
Google released its predecessor, Genie 3, as a research preview a little over a year ago. Aside from being far more photorealistic and featuring audio, Genie 4 allows for freeform edits, like changing the weather or camera angle in real time or adding new people or objects. It can maintain a consistent scene for up to two minutes, double its predecessor’s limit, and offers better physics and more human-like characters.
Gemini, Google’s AI model, is also more closely integrated with Genie 4, acting as the director that plans steps and checks frames while Genie creates the visuals. In a research experiment tied to Gemini Robotics, a Gemini 4 Argon model broke down tasks into steps that Genie 4 simulated in real time. The experiment shows a possible way to test robot scenarios in simulation before they happen in the real world.
“What we’ll increasingly see in the future are these hybrid world models, where you have a combination of Gemini writing code and text, and Genie ingesting that in real time and simulating reality at different levels of abstraction,” Tejas Kulkarni, research director at Google, said during a briefing.
As with other world models, the pitched commercial use cases include gaming, interactive learning, and robotics. One speculative example of interactive learning would be entering a painting of a historical scene and chatting to the painting’s subjects about the event portrayed.
But “trusted testers” — the people who get first access to Google cutting-edge products — are pointing to a possible new use: prototyping films.
“The real time aspect becomes most valuable in the areas where keeping a state of flow in the creativity space becomes incredibly useful,” Diego Rivas, a Google DeepMind engineer, said during a press briefing. “For example, in the ideation phase, in the storyboarding phase — anytime you’re kind of in need of rapid ideation.”
Google also offers Veo, its AI video generation model that makes high-definition clips with built-in synchronized audio from text, image, or video prompts — a tool that has been growing in popularity among filmmakers.
Rivas added that users could, eventually, rely on Gemini Omni, a multimodal large language model that can generate video from images, audio, and text, to turn those prototypes into creative assets. Though those capabilities, he says, are still a ways off.
Throughout the briefing, Rivas stressed that it’s still early days for Genie 4, and that it’s not yet clear what the end-to-end product experience will be. The team also acknowledged that Genie 4 still has gaps: details and objects can drift the longer a simulation runs, and they still haven’t quite figured out how to ensure the audio will be accurate and any in-world text will be legible.
Genie 4 is available now as a research preview for trusted testers. In the coming weeks, the model will roll out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie, Google’s AI tool for generating interactive worlds from text or image prompts, and early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

title: Carrick to stay in charge of Man Utd for Chelsea game
rawText:
Carrick to stay in charge of Man Utd for Chelsea game
- Published
Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their trip to Chelsea this weekend.
Sources have told BBC Sport that the 45-year-old will be given the opportunity to turn things around at Old Trafford following a dismal start to the campaign.
Carrick oversaw training on Tuesday morning, as United look to end a run of eight matches without a win in all competitions when they visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday.
Sunday's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford plunged Carrick's future into doubt, with United sitting one place above the relegation zone.
It is understood United's hierarchy have explored the possibility of replacing Carrick, with ex-Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann under consideration.
But sources have told BBC Sport that the former Middlesbrough manager will not only take charge against Chelsea but will also be given a chance to revive the club's fortunes on the pitch.
Carrick took interim charge in January following Ruben Amorim's departure and he was rewarded with the permanent job in May after securing Champions League qualification with an impressive run that resulted in them finishing third.
But United's form has collapsed this term, with Carrick's side winning just one of their eight Premier League matches so far this season.
Defender Lisandro Martinez criticised the club's board for a lack of investment following United's 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League earlier this month.
Captain Bruno Fernandes then took aim at Carrick's tactics following a humiliating 4-1 loss against Como in their next Champions League fixture.
The Portuguese was dropped to the bench for Sunday's loss to Bournemouth, and remained an unused substitute.
United supporters chanted Carrick's name as the former England international made his way to the tunnel after the match, but quickly directed boos at the players once Carrick had made his way off the pitch.
Carrick gestured towards the Stretford End as they chanted his name after the match.
"It wasn't a farewell from me," Carrick said on Sky Sports.
"I've mixed emotions, I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment.
"Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way. To have that connection with the supporters it's mixed emotions, it'll take a bit of time to digest but I certainly appreciate their support.
"The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough."
Carrick was at also United's training ground on Monday morning, despite the first team being given the day off.
Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada were both pictured arriving at the club's training ground on Monday, with Carrick leaving at about 17:00 GMT.
Howe, 48, is available after leaving Newcastle United last summer but any club that hires the Englishman will have to pay a multi-million pound compensation package to the Magpies after he resigned from his post with three years remaining on his deal.
Nagelsmann, 39, resigned as Germany boss following their quarter-final exit at the 2026 World Cup and is aware of United's interest in him.
Sources have also indicated Aston Villa boss Unai Emery is admired at United, but the fact he is under contract would complicate any move for the Spaniard.
Questions over Carrick remain - analysis
Manchester United might be trying to pass this off as business as usual but the reality is anything but.
The mere fact there was no clarification around Carrick's future on Monday - both before and after he was at the training ground to watch an Under-21 game his son Jacey was part of, or on Tuesday after his 07:30 arrival at Carrington and the 11:00 training start time, fuels theories and speculation, which just adds to the air of uncertainty.
Carrick will be in charge at Stamford Bridge, but what about Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and Aston Villa after that?
Given the woeful nature of their last two performances, how will United's players respond at Chelsea when the spotlight on them is so fierce? Can Carrick drag a performance out of them? Has he made his peace with skipper Bruno Fernandes?
Is director of football Jason Wilcox safe? There are still so many unanswered questions.
Last season's win at Stamford Bridge was one of the key results in securing Carrick the head coach's job permanently. Will the next trip there be the start of a brighter future or mark the end of his tenure?

title: The secret to slower aging may be hiding in your gut
rawText:
The secret to slower aging may be hiding in your gut
- Date:
- October 27, 2026
- Source:
- University of Hawaii at Manoa
- Summary:
- The secret to aging more slowly may be hiding in your gut. Scientists discovered that certain gut bacteria are strongly linked to how quickly the body ages, with microbial differences accounting for about 15% of the variation in biological aging rates. Some bacterial species were associated with slower aging, while others were linked to accelerated aging.
- Share:
Scientists have uncovered a surprising connection between the bacteria living in the human gut and the speed at which the body ages. Researchers at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa found that certain gut microbes are associated with slower biological aging, while others are linked to faster aging.
The study, published in Scientific Reports, found that differences in gut bacterial communities accounted for approximately 15% of the variation in participants' biological aging rates. The results suggest that the gut microbiome, the vast community of microorganisms living in the digestive system, may provide valuable clues about aging at the molecular level.
"This study advances our understanding of the relationship between the gut microbiome and biological aging," said senior author Alika K. Maunakea of the UH Mānoa John A. Burns School of Medicine. "We found that microbial patterns in the gut were significantly associated with molecular measures of aging, even independent of chronological age. These findings open important new directions for understanding how modifiable biological systems influence long-term health trajectories and longevity."
Scientists Identify Gut Bacteria Linked to Faster and Slower Aging
To investigate the relationship between gut bacteria and aging, researchers examined stool and blood samples collected from 123 adults across a wide range of ages. They identified the bacteria present in each participant's gut and compared those findings with blood-based molecular markers used to estimate the body's rate of aging.
These biological measurements differ from chronological age, which simply reflects how many years someone has been alive. Instead, they are designed to assess how quickly aging-related changes are occurring within the body.
The researchers found a notable association between the composition of the gut microbiome and DunedinPACE, an advanced biomarker that measures the pace of biological aging.
Some bacterial species stood out for their particularly strong relationships with aging. Bifidobacterium adolescentis was among the microbes most strongly associated with slower biological aging. In contrast, Succinivibrio dextrinosolvens showed one of the strongest associations with faster aging.
These differences suggest that particular patterns of gut bacteria may offer important information about how rapidly the body is aging.
How Diet, Lifestyle, and Environment May Influence Gut Health
Lead author Braden P. Kunihiro said the discovery adds to growing evidence that the gut microbiome could play an important role in precision health research, which aims to better understand individual differences in health and disease.
Unlike chronological age, the composition of the gut microbiome can change in response to everyday influences, including diet, lifestyle, and environmental conditions. This makes it a particularly interesting area of investigation for scientists studying healthy aging.
"The gut microbiome is highly responsive to lifestyle, diet, environment and other everyday exposures," Kunihiro said. "Our findings suggest that the microbiome may reflect important aspects of biological resilience and aging in ways that could eventually help inform future wellness and healthy aging strategies."
The research also included Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander participants, groups that have historically received limited representation in studies of aging and gut microorganisms.
Co-author Ruben Juarez explained that including these populations could help scientists investigate how social circumstances and environmental conditions leave lasting biological effects over the course of a person's life.
"The microbiome exists at the intersection of behavior, environment and human biology," Juarez said. "Studies like this help illuminate potential pathways through which lived experiences and social factors influence long-term health outcomes."
Could Changing Gut Bacteria Influence How We Age?
Although the findings reveal a meaningful relationship between gut bacteria and biological aging, researchers stress that the study does not establish cause and effect. In other words, finding certain microbes in people who age more slowly does not necessarily mean those bacteria are responsible for slowing the aging process.
Further studies will be needed to determine whether deliberately changing the gut microbiome can influence biological aging or improve long-term health.
Still, the findings offer a promising starting point for exploring how the microorganisms living inside us relate to the aging process and whether they could eventually help guide more personalized approaches to healthy aging.
"This is an important early step toward understanding the gut microbiome's relationship with healthy aging," Maunakea said. "Future research will help clarify the mechanisms involved and whether these microbial signatures may eventually contribute to precision approaches for promoting long-term health and wellness."

title: Low testosterone may make sugar far more harmful to your liver
rawText:
Low testosterone may make sugar far more harmful to your liver
- Date:
- October 27, 2026
- Source:
- Osaka Metropolitan University
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered that low testosterone and a high-fructose diet can work together to worsen fatty liver disease in mice. Unexpectedly, changes in gut bacteria appear to drive this harmful interaction, revealing a potential new target for preventing liver damage.
- Share:
Low testosterone can contribute to several health problems, and an unhealthy diet may make some of those risks even worse. One major concern is metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), a condition that affects approximately 40% of adult men worldwide and has become a significant global health issue.
Fatty liver, the earliest stage of MASLD, occurs when excess fat builds up in the liver. Several factors are associated with the condition, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, low testosterone levels, and excessive fructose consumption from sugary drinks and processed foods. However, scientists have not fully understood how these factors interact or whether their combined effects are more harmful than each one individually.
How Low Testosterone and Fructose Affect the Liver
To investigate this connection, a research team from the Graduate School of Agriculture, led by graduate student Hiroki Takahashi and Associate Professor Naoki Harada, examined how reduced testosterone and high fructose intake influence liver health.
The researchers used eight-week-old male mice and divided them into six experimental groups. Some underwent castration to lower testosterone levels, while others received a sham operation. The groups included Sham/Control, Sham/Fructose, Sham/Fructose + Antibiotics, Castration/Control, Castration/Fructose, and Castration/Fructose + Antibiotics.
To determine how these conditions affected the animals, the team analyzed liver cells and tissues, blood plasma, organic acids from the cecum, and samples of gut bacteria.
A Dangerous Combination for Fatty Liver
The results revealed that mice with reduced testosterone levels developed heavier livers when they consumed fructose. However, this increase in liver weight was smaller in mice that also received antibiotics.
When examined separately, low testosterone and fructose intake produced only modest changes in liver triglyceride levels. When combined, however, the two factors had a much stronger effect, significantly increasing fat accumulation and worsening fatty liver.
The researchers also identified changes in the composition of gut bacteria, altered liver gene activity, and elevated levels of pyruvate in the cecum among mice exposed to both reduced testosterone and fructose.
These findings suggested that the gut microbiome could play an important role in explaining why the combination was particularly harmful.
Gut Bacteria Reveal a Hidden Mechanism
Further experiments helped the researchers identify a possible biological explanation for the increased liver fat.
"Upon examining this mechanism, we found that changes in the gut microbiota led to increased levels of pyruvate within the intestine. Furthermore, experiments using mouse-derived primary hepatocytes revealed that pyruvate acts synergistically with fructose to promote neutral lipid accumulation in hepatocytes," explained Takahashi.
In other words, changes in gut bacteria appeared to increase intestinal pyruvate, a compound involved in energy metabolism. Laboratory experiments with liver cells isolated from mice showed that pyruvate and fructose worked together to increase fat storage in those cells.
The discovery suggests that interactions among testosterone levels, dietary fructose, and gut bacteria may help explain how fatty liver develops and worsens.
Potential New Ways to Prevent Fatty Liver Disease
Understanding this relationship could eventually help researchers identify new approaches to preventing or treating fatty liver disease. In particular, targeting the processes through which pyruvate contributes to fat accumulation may offer promising possibilities.
"Going forward, we hope to clarify the mechanism by which pyruvate promotes triglyceride accumulation to pioneer the development of therapeutic drugs and establishment of preventive methods through dietary interventions," added Professor Harada.
Although the findings come from experiments in mice and isolated mouse liver cells, they provide new insight into how hormonal changes and diet may interact to influence liver health.
The study was published in American Journal of Physiology-Endocrinology and Metabolism.

title: Un analista internacional explicó en detalle la remontada histórica de Lula y las dudas que generó el voto electrónico: “Llama la atención”
rawText:
Andrés Repetto habló en LN+ sobre las claves del triunfo del mandatario brasileño y la controversia por la extensión del horario de votación; diferenció los cuestionamientos de Flavio Bolsonaro de una eventual irregularidad en el sistema de urnas
- 5 minutos de lectura'
La victoria de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva frente a Flavio Bolsonaro dejó un escenario de fuerte tensión política en Brasil. La remontada del líder del Partido de los Trabajadores (PT), las dificultades de transporte durante la jornada y la decisión judicial de extender el horario de votación quedaron en el centro del debate. En LN+, el analista internacional Andrés Repetto examinó los factores que favorecieron al oficialismo y los argumentos del candidato opositor para desconocer el resultado.
“Sorprendido, pero no tanto”, expresó al comienzo de su intervención. Para el especialista, el desenlace volvió a poner bajo cuestionamiento a las encuestadoras y mostró la importancia de movilizar a los electores. Al mismo tiempo, advirtió que la controversia sobre la organización de los comicios requiere distinguir entre los problemas para llegar a los centros de votación, la prórroga dispuesta por la Justicia y el funcionamiento de las urnas electrónicas.
Aunque describió el resultado como “contundente” y “claro”, Repetto señaló que la aplicación de la extensión horaria abrió interrogantes que Bolsonaro utilizó para impugnar la elección. Sus observaciones, sin embargo, no constituyeron una comprobación de fraude.
La movilización que favoreció la remontada de Lula
Uno de los puntos centrales del análisis fue la capacidad del PT para llevar más votantes a las urnas. Repetto recordó que, durante los días previos, había planteado que una mayor participación podía favorecer al presidente brasileño.
“Si Lula logra movilizar más cantidad de gente, eso lo puede beneficiar, y es lo que pasó”, sostuvo. Desde su perspectiva, esa capacidad de convocatoria fue una de las claves para entender el desenlace de la segunda vuelta.
El triunfo revirtió el orden de la primera vuelta, en la que Flavio Bolsonaro había terminado por delante de Lula, según los datos del Tribunal Superior Electoral.
Repetto también dirigió sus críticas a los sondeos. “Una vez más, las encuestas fallaron”, afirmó, y cuestionó la influencia que pueden ejercer sobre las expectativas del electorado y las decisiones de las campañas.
La falta de colectivos y la extensión de la votación
La controversia que describió el analista comenzó con las dificultades para trasladarse a los centros electorales. Según explicó, durante el mediodía el PT reclamó una intervención ante la falta de colectivos, un problema que podía afectar especialmente a los votantes de las periferias y del norte del país.
Repetto agregó que Bolsonaro también había solicitado medidas vinculadas con las condiciones climáticas. En ese contexto, ubicó la decisión judicial de prolongar la jornada electoral por dos horas.
El punto que consideró más sensible fue el momento en que se comunicó la medida. Según su reconstrucción, la orden llegó cuando las urnas electrónicas ya habían cerrado, lo que generó incertidumbre sobre cómo podía aplicarse la extensión.
“Cuando dan la orden para que se estire el proceso de votación, la dan desde la Justicia tarde, la orden llega tarde”, sostuvo. Para el especialista, allí se encontraba uno de los principales motivos del conflicto: determinar cuántas personas habían tenido dificultades para movilizarse y cuántas finalmente no pudieron votar.
Qué cuestionó Repetto sobre las urnas electrónicas
Al referirse al sistema de votación, Repetto puso el foco en la coordinación entre la decisión judicial y el cierre de los dispositivos. “Teniendo un voto electrónico, ¿cómo puede ser que vos lo estires dos horas más, tres horas más?”, planteó durante el intercambio.
Su interrogante apuntó a la implementación de la prórroga. Más adelante, diferenció expresamente ese problema de las acusaciones sobre una supuesta reapertura de las urnas.
“Lo que dice Bolsonaro, que se abrieron las urnas, es imposible abrir las urnas electrónicas”, afirmó. Y precisó: “Una cosa es el tema de las urnas electrónicas y otra lo que pasó con los micros y la prolongación de la votación”.
También recordó que durante la transmisión de los resultados hubo proyecciones tempranas. Según relató, una de las cadenas brasileñas anticipaba un triunfo de Lula con alrededor del 14% de los votos escrutados, a partir de cálculos matemáticos.
El rechazo de Bolsonaro y la respuesta internacional
Durante el programa se difundió una declaración de Flavio Bolsonaro en la que anunció que recurriría a la Justicia para pedir la anulación de los comicios. El candidato argumentó que desconocía cuántos votos podría haber obtenido en los lugares donde, según su planteo, no se había aplicado la extensión.
Repetto comparó esa reacción con la de Jair Bolsonaro tras la elección anterior, aunque marcó una diferencia política: en aquella oportunidad, quien cuestionaba el resultado todavía ejercía la presidencia.
En paralelo, destacó las señales de reconocimiento que recibió Lula desde distintos espacios ideológicos. Para el analista, esas manifestaciones reflejaban el peso de Brasil y la necesidad de sostener relaciones entre gobiernos más allá de sus afinidades partidarias.
“Izquierda, derecha, lo importante es el diálogo y entender que Brasil es una potencia y que se tiene que trabajar con Brasil”, cerró.

title: Gabriel Rolón, psicoanalista: “La gracia del amor es abrazar también la imperfección del otro”
rawText:
En una entrevista exclusiva para LN+, el psicoanalista y escritor reflexionó sobre la naturaleza humana y propuso una mirada cruda sobre el amor, la muerte y la persistencia de los mandatos sociales
- 4 minutos de lectura'
En una entrevista para LN+ Gabriel Rolón se refirió a los vínculos de pareja: “Tengo una mala noticia: una mañana te vas a dar vuelta vas a mirar la sábana y vas a ver que de tu media naranja caen chorros de desilusión, porque a toda media naranja le falta al menos un gajo, porque esa ilusión de completud no está”, sostuvo en diálogo con Luis Novaresio.
“¿Qué gracia tiene amar a alguien que es perfecto? La gracia del amor es abrazar también la imperfección del otro. Es el lugar donde el otro no puede (...) entender que el otro, como yo, es un ser recorrido por la falta, por el miedo, por la angustia", explicó
El especialista se refirió al concepto de la “VTV del amor”, una metáfora sobre la necesidad de revisar periódicamente el estado de las relaciones. “La mayoría de las personas tienen desgraciadamente parejas que no querrían tener, o porque no han terminado de aceptar eso que de su pareja no les gusta y sufren, o porque ya está, se han resignado”, destacó el especialista.
En este contexto, sostuvo que el miedo a la soledad es un factor determinante que empuja a muchos individuos a sostener vínculos dañinos, donde olvidan que la soledad es una condición intrínseca de ser seres hablantes.
“Nos acostumbramos y terminamos en el amor transitando sin rueda de auxilio, sin matafuegos, con el vehículo del amor un poco averiado”, reafirmó y explicó que muchas personas mantienen sus relaciones por miedo.
“El miedo a la soledad es intrínseca al ser humano, porque también en esos momentos en los que vos te podés resguardar, hasta abrazando a la persona que amás, después de un rato vas a sentir que te calmaste un montón, pero seguís sintiendo esa soledad que te recorre”, concluyó.
El deseo
Durante la entrevista, el reconcido psicoanalista Gabriel Rolón profundizó en las aristas más complejas del comportamiento humano y puso el foco en cómo la incomodidad es un componente ineludible para quien decide profundizar en su propia subjetividad.
“El deseo te incomoda porque te señala la falta. Se desea lo que no se tiene”, afirmó el analista y en la misma línea sumó: “Cuando surge el deseo, ya es algo incómodo. Ya uno empieza a ponerse de lo que sea, desde: `No habrá un vaso de agua por acá?` hasta: `¿Dónde está la persona que alguna vez me amará?`“.
Asimismo, el escritor comparó el deseo como iluminación que señala la falta: “El deseo va a ser ese foco de luz que te ilumina, ni más ni menos que ese lugar donde hay algo que te falta. Entonces ya de por sí es incómodo”
“Vas a empezar a caminar alrededor de eso que te falta, buscándole algunos semblantes. Un amor, un libro, un éxito, un programa de televisión, un trabajo, un hijo. Lo que vos quieras que son todos nobles intentos de llenar un vacío imposible de ser llenado”, agregó para remarcar que convivir con la falta es una condición propia del ser humano.
“Eso es ser un ser humano; es vivir con el sentimiento trágico de la vida, que sé que me voy a morir, sé que todos los que amo se van a morir, sé que todo lo que amo en algún momento no estará. Tengo que vivir con eso, sabiéndolo”, reafirmó en la misma línea.

title: UK sanctions Sudanese military leaders implicated in El Fasher ‘campaign of rape’
rawText:
Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a mass atrocity that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days.
A year after the fall of El Fasher, the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city.
A total of 15 commanders from the military groups – the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) – have been subjected to a travel ban and an asset freeze.
The Foreign Office said it hoped the action would ensure “the horrors that took place at El Fasher will be known to the world”.
During the RSF’s takeover of the city, up to 10,000 men, women and children are believed to have been slaughtered over two days – the fastest and largest massacre of civilians this century. Another 40,000 remain unaccounted for.
The killings came at the end of an 18-month starvation siege by the RSF, which was allegedly backed by the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The UAE continues to deny supporting the RSF.
Fewer than 70,000 people are believed to remain in El Fasher, compared with a prewar population of more than 1 million. Life inside the city continues to be horrendous, with testimony indicating routine detention, torture and unlawful killings.
Individuals targeted by the UK’s latest sanctions include Hussein Abu Jalak, an RSF colonel linked to atrocities during the siege, which forced hundreds of thousands of civilians to live off animal feed.
Another is Al-Nour Ahmed Adam – also known as “Al-Qubba” – who was identified as playing a prominent role in the attack on the city.
A Guardian investigation earlier this year revealed internal US and UK warnings were sidelined in the run-up to the RSF attack on El Fasher, and that action that might have saved lives was not taken.
A statement to mark the anniversary of the massacre from the Coalition on Atrocity Prevention and Justice for Sudan said: “The victims will not be forgotten, survivors will be heard, and we will continue to pursue accountability for those responsible.”
During the 12 months since the fall of El Fasher, Sudan’s ruinous conflict – which has forced 14 million people to flee their homes – has developed increasingly into a drone war.
The latest strikes saw the RSF causing mass power outages across east Sudan after targeting power stations with a coordinated drone attack.

title: ‘Tomó una buena decisión’: Sheinbaum ‘palomea’ renuncia de Guadalupe Taddei al INE
rawText:
La presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum ‘palomeó’ la renuncia de Guadalupe Taddei, consejera presidenta del Instituto Nacional Electoral (INE) y aseguró que se harán las auditorías correspondientes para conocer las supuestas irregularidades.
La mandataria admitió que la salida de Taddei ocurre en un momento polémico rumbo a las elecciones 2027, pero aseguró que hay una Ley Electoral que establece las reglas para elegir al nuevo consejero presidente del INE.
“No podía haber esa sombra de conflicto de interés en el INE y procede lo que viene, está en la ley”, agregó la presidenta quien recordó que corresponderá al Congreso abrir el proceso para renovar dicho cargo.
Sheinbaum reacciona a renuncia de Guadalupe Taddei en el INE
La presidenta Sheinbaum calificó como una “buena decisión” la que tomó Guadalupe Taddei de renunciar a su cargo como consejera presidenta del INE.
“Taddei toma la decisión de separarse del cargo frente a los señalamientos que había, pero tiene que hacer la investigación, tiene que haber una auditoría para revisar las sospechas o señalamientos que ha habido sobre los abusos del INE”.
La mandataria reiteró que no es posible permitir los lujos ni los excesos en México, sobre todo de servidores públicos. Al mismo tiempo criticó los comentarios y los calificó como “misóginos” sobre quienes se refirieron a la vida personal de Taddei.
“Ella tomó una buena decisión al separarse del cargo. Es muy cobarde y misógino agredir a una mujer, no lo que hizo como servidora pública sino por motivos personales. Tendrá que decidirse en los próximos días quién estará al frente del INE y abrir el proceso”, agregó la mandataria.
Sheinbaum responde a oposición que exige ‘cero impunidad’ contra Taddei: ‘El chiste se cuenta solo’
Luego de la exigencia de los partidos de oposición para que haya “cero impunidad” en contra de Guadalupe Taddei, la presidenta se ‘burló’ de dichas críticas e intenciones.
“Imagínense al presidente del PRI hablando de honestidad, es un chiste que se cuenta solo. No podemos cerrar la idea con que ahora la derecha es honesta”.
La mandataria hizo un llamado también a que el Congreso elija a la persona ideal para que quede al frente del INE rumbo al proceso electoral de 2027.
“Es importante lo que pasó, hubo un señalamiento por conflicto de interés y que se investigue. Es mejor que la persona se separe para que se pueda hacer bien la investigación y que la Auditoría señale si está involucrada o no”, agregó.
Calendario de la Pensión Bienestar: ¿Cuándo inicia el pago del bimestre noviembre-diciembre?
Leticia Ramírez, secretaria del Bienestar, dio a conocer el calendario de la Pensión Bienestar para el bimestre noviembre-diciembre. Se trata del último depósito del año y comenzará a partir del martes 3 de noviembre.
Dichos depósitos se realizarán en orden alfabético según la primera letra del apellido paterno y comenzarán tras el feriado del Día de Muertos. Estas son las fechas:
Sheinbaum anuncia revisión del ISSSTE a partir de hoy
La presidenta Sheinbaum anunció que a partir de este lunes iniciará la revisión en el Instituto de Seguridad y Servicios Sociales para los Trabajadores del Estado (ISSSTE) para saber qué necesidades tienen en el sistema de salud.
“Iniciará la revisión de las condiciones del ISSSTE para saber cuánto personal requiere y la infraestructura porque en todo el periodo neoliberal se quedó abandonado”, añadió la mandataria.
¿Por qué los transportistas bloquean carreteras HOY?
Al iniciar su conferencia, la presidenta Sheinbaum adelantó que a las 11:00 horas habrá una reunión entre los transportistas, la Secretaría de Hacienda y la Secretaría de Gobernación, para aclarar el malentendido sobre la reducción en la deducción del ISR por el pago de peaje, que pasó de 300 a 250 millones de pesos
Los transportistas anunciaron un paro nacional para este lunes en distintos puntos carreteros del país. La principal exigencia son acciones en materia de seguridad, para mejorar el mal estado de carreteras y la modificación de la Ley de Ingresos que reduce el beneficio fiscal a empresas.
Hacienda explicó que la doble reducción en el ISR en el pago del peaje afecta solo a 170 empresas, lo que representa solo el 6 por ciento del sector.
“Es un sector muy pequeñito el que se ve afectado y en temas de seguridad hay una mesa permanente con la Secretaría de Gobernación”, dijo la mandataria.
Sheinbaum festeja triunfo de Lula en Brasil: ‘Es una bocanada de aire fresco para América Latina’
La presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum inició su conferencia diciendo: “Estamos muy contentos por el triunfo de Lula en Brasil”.
“Es una bocanada de aire fresco para América Latina. Es un triunfo muy importante del pueblo de Brasil”, agregó la mandataria.
Sheinbaum agregó que se trató del triunfo de un presidente que representa a su pueblo y se impuso a Bolsonaro durante la segunda vuelta en los comicios.
La mandaria dijo que tendrá una llamada con Lula da Silva a las 12:00 horas de este lunes para felicitarlo y añadió que mantendrán los proyectos conjuntos.

title: Los gráficos que explican la inédita remontada de Lula en las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil
rawText:
Los gráficos que explican la inédita remontada de Lula en las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil
  - Autor, Luiz Fernando Toledo y Thais Carrança*
  - Título del autor, BBC News Brasil en Londres y Sao Paulo
- Fecha de publicación
- Tiempo de lectura: 4 min
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva logró un cuarto mandato inédito y este domingo se convirtió en el primer candidato a la presidencia en la historia de Brasil en lograr una remontada entre la primera y la segunda vuelta.
Con el 99,98% de las mesas electorales escrutadas, el aspirante a la reelección obtuvo el 51,78% de los votos válidos (64.241.786), frente al 48,22% del derechista Flávio Bolsonaro, quien sumó 59.818.887 sufragios, reportó el Tribunal Superior Electoral (TSE).
En la primera vuelta, celebrada el 4 de octubre, el presidente había quedado en segundo lugar con 53.879.538 votos (45,16%), por detrás de Bolsonaro, quien recibió 56.104.503 (47,03%).
La diferencia de 2,2 millones de votos a favor del candidato del Partido Liberal (PL) se transformó en una ventaja de 4,4 millones de sufragios para Lula en la segunda vuelta.
El candidato del Partido de los Trabajadores (PT) sumó 10.376.694 votos más que los obtenidos en la primera contienda. Bolsonaro, por su parte, también incrementó su votación, pero a un ritmo menor, y obtuvo 3.721.538 nuevas papeletas.
Los datos oficiales muestran que el triunfo de Lula fue el resultado de una remontada en el estado de Minas Gerais, de una reducción de su desventaja en los grandes colegios electorales del sudeste y de una ampliación de su ventaja en los estados del nordeste.
Lula aumentó su porcentaje de votos válidos en los 26 estados y en el Distrito Federal en comparación con la primera vuelta.
El giro de Minas Gerais y la sorpresa de Sao Paulo
Minas Gerais, en el sureste de Brasil, fue el único estado donde se produjo un cambio de tendencia entre la primera y la segunda vuelta. En la primera ronda, Bolsonaro se impuso en el estado con 5.777.548 votos (48,24%), frente a los 5.188.936 obtenidos por Lula (43,33%).
Sin embargo, en el balotaje, con el 99,83% de las mesas escrutadas, Lula obtuvo 6.351.099 votos (50,43%), frente a los 6.241.786 (49,57%). de Bolsonaro.
Este cambio llevó a Lula de ocupar el primer lugar en 13 estados frente a los 12 que ganó en la primera vuelta, mientras que su rival pasó de ganar en 15 y a 14.
En Sao Paulo fue el estado en el que Lula sumó la mayor cantidad de votos, allí pasó de 9.505.413 votos (38,20%) a 12.119.274 (46,15%), un aumento de 2.613.861 votos, con el 100% de las mesas escrutadas.
A pesar de este avance, Lula quedó por detrás de Bolsonaro en el estado.
El candidato del PL consiguió 12.922.023 votos (51,93%) en la primera vuelta, mientras que en la segunda 14.139.178 (53,85%).
Su ventaja, que era de 3.416.610 votos, cayó a 2.019.904. La reducción de 1.396.706 votos en esa diferencia fue la mayor entre todos los estados.
En Río de Janeiro se presentó una situación similar. Lula había recibido 3.693.021 votos (39,41%) en la primera vuelta, pero consiguió a 4.565.286 (46,90%) en la segunda. Por su parte, Bolsonaro mantuvo el liderazgo, con un 53,10%, pero su ventaja se redujo de 1.273.823 a 603.616 votos.
Aunque conseguir más sufragios en un estado no significó la victoria de Lula en el mismo, esto contribuyó al vuelco a nivel nacional al reducir la brecha con su rival derechista.
El Nordeste, el bastión consolidado
Lula mantuvo el liderazgo en los nueve estados del nordeste de Brasil y aumentó su votación en todos ellos. Al sumar los resultados estatales disponibles, el candidato del PT obtuvo 2,95 millones de sufragios más que en la primera vuelta.
Bahía fue el estado que aportó el mayor incremento en términos absolutos dentro de la región.
Lula pasó de 5.664.771 votos (66,17%) a 6.484.995 (71,31%), con el 99,99% de las mesas escrutadas. Bolsonaro, por su parte, también sumó votos, pero esto no impidió que la brecha con su rival aumentara.
En Pernambuco, Lula pasó del 63,45% al 69,20% de los votos. En Ceará, pasó del 63,29% al 68,93% y en Piauí, donde ya contaba con el 70,99% en la primera vuelta, alcanzó el 75,88%, según los cómputos oficiales.
En el Distrito Federal, Lula también avanzó y pasó de conseguir el 38,11% de las papeletas al 45,72%, pero continuó por detrás de su adversario.
En Amapá, que registró la votación más ajustada de la primera vuelta, Lula pasó del 45,71 % al 52,88 % de los votos.
El presidente ya había quedado en primer lugar en el estado durante la primera votación, pero con apenas 225 votos: 212.503 frente a los 212.278 de Bolsonaro.
De perder a ganar en 211 municipios
Lula pasó de perder a ganar en 211 municipios entre las dos vueltas de la elección.
Este giro incluyó a dos capitales: Río de Janeiro y Macapá, así como ciudades densamente pobladas de las regiones metropolitanas de Sao Paulo, Belo Horizonte y Belén.
En Río de Janeiro, el candidato del PT pasó del 43,91% al 51,54% de los votos válidos. Tras terminar la primera vuelta 137.837 votos por detrás de Bolsonaro, Lula cerró la segunda con una ventaja de 113.193 votos.
Bolsonaro ha anunciado que impugnará los resultados.
"Es imposible reconocer el resultado de las elecciones", dijo el senador, quien criticó la extensión del horario de votación.
El magistrado del Supremo Tribunal Federal, Cristiano Zanin, ordenó ampliar en dos horas el horario de votación en todo el país, accediendo a una solicitud de la campaña de Lula, la cual explicó que las autoridades de varias ciudades estaban restringiendo el acceso de los votantes al transporte público.
Bolsonaro calificó la decisión de Zanin como "inaceptable", a pesar de que él también solicitó tiempo adicional en tres estados, alegando el mal tiempo.
Gráficos a cargo de Caroline Souza, del equipo de Periodismo Visual de BBC News Brasil.

title: Calendario de pagos de Pensión del Bienestar: ¿Cuándo inician depósitos del bimestre noviembre-diciembre?
rawText:
El Gobierno de México empezará la distribución del último pago de 2026 de la Pensión para las personas adultas mayores el próximo martes 3 de noviembre, adelantó Leticia Ramírez, secretaría del Bienestar.
El calendario, presentado en Palacio Nacional, también aplica para la Pensión Mujeres Bienestar, un programa creado por la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum en este sexenio y que se entrega a mexicanas de entre 60 a 64 años.
Leticia Ramírez enfatizó que este es el calendario “real” de pagos, esto después de que la Secretaría del Bienestar ha denunciado en semanas recientes publicaciones falsas sobre los programas sociales del Gobierno.
Dime tu apellido y te diré cuándo te depositan la Pensión del Bienestar en noviembre
Los beneficiarios cuyo apellido paterno inicia con A serán los primeros en recibir el depósito de 6 mil 400 pesos. La dispersión de los recursos terminará el próximo viernes 27 de noviembre.
Los días de depósito de las Pensiones del Bienestar quedan de la siguiente manera:
El depósito de la Pensión del Bienestar solo se suspenderá el próximo lunes 16 de noviembre por el feriado del Aniversario de la Revolución Mexicana.
Programas del Bienestar: ¿De cuánto son los pagos?
La pensión que da más dinero es la que se entrega a las personas adultas mayores de 65 años en adelante, con un depósito de 6 mil 400 pesos.
Los pagos de los Programas del Bienestar del Gobierno son los siguientes:
- Pensión Mujeres Bienestar: 3 mil 100 pesos cada dos meses.
- Pensión para personas con discapacidad: 3 mil 300 pesos bimestrales.
- Apoyo para madres trabajadoras: 1 mil 650 pesos por hijo o hija cada dos meses.
- Sembrando Vida: 6 mil 400 pesos por su jornal mensual. El pago se depositará a todos los beneficiarios el miércoles 11 de noviembre.
“No es necesario que ustedes retiren su dinero el día en que se realiza el depósito porque los recursos están disponible siempre en su Tarjeta del Bienestar y los pueden utilizar el día que los necesiten”, subrayó Leticia Ramírez.
¿Cómo puedes ubicar tu Banco del Bienestar más cercano?
Recuerda que si bien puedes sacar el dinero de tu pensión en cualquier cajero, si lo haces en aquellos que no sean del Banco del Bienestar se te cobrará una comisión cada vez que hagas un retiro.
Para saber dónde está la sucursal más cercana, ingresa a esta liga de la Secretaría del Bienestar. Después selecciona en qué estado de la República vives y da clic en buscar. La página desplegará una lista con todas las ubicaciones en tu lugar.
El horario de servicio de las sucursales del Banco del Bienestar es de lunes a viernes de 9 de la mañana a 4:30 de la tarde.

title: Anthropic reveals $80 billion loss, huge spending spree ahead of IPO
rawText:
Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic on Monday unveiled its public IPO filing for the first time ahead of what is expected to be one of the largest stock debuts in history.
That offering, widely expected to come sometime in mid-November, could value the Claude developer at more than $2 trillion. That could surpass the current record holder, Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in an IPO in June that valued the rocket-AI-social media firm at $2.1 trillion.
The filing did not include a potential share price, the number of shares to be offered or a valuation for the whole company, all of which will be determined after Anthropic holds a “roadshow” with investors, prospective investors and its bankers.
Monday’s filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission showed that Anthropic, like other AI firms, is splashing out unprecedented amounts of cash on cloud services to run its AI models.
The company plans to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon for cloud services through April 2036, and another $120 billion with SpaceX through 2029.
Anthropic also said it planned to spend $115 billion with Google and $45 billion with Microsoft, both through 2033, for computing infrastructure.
The filing said that the company recorded revenue growth of “1,368% year over year for the three months ended June 30, 2026.”
The cost of renting servers and chips grew by 300% over the same period.
Anthropic’s net loss for the first six months of 2026 was $80.7 billion. For the entirety of 2025, the company reported a $42 billion net loss.
Anthropic added that it expects its current cash and sales to be sufficient for the next 12 months, but warned that future revenue growth depends on a number of important factors, including the cost of infrastructure. As a result, it said “we may be required to seek additional financing sooner than we currently anticipate.”
The company said it has raised about $141 billion of capital through the end of June and is currently sitting on $112.4 billion of cash.
The company plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT.” Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the historic offering, as they did with SpaceX’s record deal.
But already, the offering is coming slightly later than expected as recent market moves give investors pause about the trajectory of the seemingly ever-expanding AI boom.
Monday’s filing is unlikely to calm those fears.
Alongside its dramatic spending and borrowing figures, Anthropic warned that it “may not generate sufficient revenue to achieve or sustain profitability in the future.”
“While we have experienced significant revenue growth in recent periods, our business is highly capital intensive,” the company said. “Our revenue growth may not be sustainable, and our rate of growth may decrease.”
Nevertheless, Anthropic told regulators and investors that it plans to keep burning through capital. “We expect our costs will increase over time and our losses will continue as we expect to invest significant resources towards growing our business and operating as a public company.”
On Sunday, a top Wall Street economist warned that the sector had yet to deliver broad gains to the wider economy.
“Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” said Torsten Slok, chief economist at investment firm Apollo Global Management.
“Profit margins are rising for the Mag 7 but are flat for the S&P 493,” he wrote on Sunday, referring to the companies left in the benchmark S&P 500 after subtracting for Meta, Microsoft, Alphabet, Apple, Amazon, Nvidia and Tesla. “ And there are still no signs of AI boosting productivity growth.”
The Nasdaq 100 which tracks the largest public AI developers, is up 15% this year. That’s more than the broader S&P 500’s 11% gain so far this year.
Market jitters over potential cracks in the AI boom have also caused a number of smaller IPOs to put their plans on hold. Earlier this month, a number of small offerings delayed or canceled their plans to go public, citing “market conditions.”
But still, the largest AI companies continue to raise massive amounts of funding for their projects. On Monday, Meta Platforms announced an up to $95 billion stock offering, while SpaceX said it had secured $40 billion in funding to buy Nvidia graphics processing units, which it called the largest type of fundraising ever.
As part of every stock offering, companies are asked to outline risks and uncertainties facing its business. Some of the risk factors outlined by Anthropic included safety, reliable computing infrastructure and its ability to “navigate an evolving, uncertain, and at times divergent global regulatory landscape.”
“Concerns have been raised both within our organization and by other researchers, regulators, policymakers, and industry participants that sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity,” the filing said.
Some of those potential risks have manifested themselves recently, as the firms have faced intense scrutiny over a swath of incidents in which their models and agents have hacked into government and private websites and services.
The companies, including Anthropic, have said they’re taking steps to bolster security. But those incidents also came as Anthropic founder Dario Amodei in September wrote that companies should “pace the frontier,” a way of saying that AI models were advancing faster than humans could grasp their capabilities.
Some within the industry conditionally agreed with Amodei, but Washington sharply rebuked the idea. He and President Donald Trump met privately and again at an industry meeting that took place at the White House.
